subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Peak-End Rule
description: A 60-second lesson on The Peak-End Rule.

hook.text: A painful medical procedure ending gently is remembered as less painful than a shorter, sharper one.

buildup.text: Kahneman's peak-end rule: we judge experiences by their most intense moment and how they ended.

discovery.text: Duration barely matters. A 30-minute ordeal with a gentle end beats a 10-minute one with a harsh end.

twist.text: Disney knows this: the fireworks are at the end. Your last memory is the one that sticks.

climax.text: This splits us into two selves: the experiencing self who lives it and the remembering self who judges it.

punchline.text: End well. That's what gets remembered.

quiz.question: What does the peak-end rule predict?
options: We judge experiences by peak intensity and ending
Duration is the key factor in memory

details.summary: People evaluate past experiences based primarily on how they felt at the peak intensity moment and at the end, rather than averaging the entire experience. A painful medical procedure with a gentle ending is remembered more favorably than a shorter procedure with an abrupt painful end.
details.whyItMatters: The peak-end rule shapes how memories form and drives future choices. It has transformed how medical procedures, customer experiences, and vacations are designed.
takeaways: Evaluations depend on the peak moment and the ending
Duration of the experience has surprisingly little impact
Kahneman demonstrated the rule with cold water experiments

faq.question: What was Kahneman's cold water experiment?
faq.answer: Participants held a hand in painfully cold water for 60 seconds, then in another trial for 60 seconds followed by 30 seconds of slightly warmer water. They preferred the longer trial because it ended better, even though it involved more total pain. Duration was neglected.

faq.question: How can businesses use the peak-end rule?
faq.answer: Ensure the final moment of a customer interaction is positive: a warm goodbye, a small gift, or a smooth checkout. Create one memorable peak moment rather than an evenly mediocre experience. These strategies improve satisfaction ratings more than incremental improvements throughout.
